SMTO-HTTP-0053 — The Gateway is missing software it needs for web requests

GUID: 3d708eaf-0365-4a40-84d4-bd36c12561fe
Slug: http-gateway-dependency-missing
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Part of the Gateway's installation is missing, so it can't make web requests until it is repaired. Nothing was sent to the other service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the computer running this Gateway to run its SMTO installer again there, using the same account the Gateway runs as. The installer puts back the missing software and keeps the Gateway's pairing and settings.
  2. When no tasks are running on that Gateway, restart it, then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that it shows Connected. The Gateway only loads the repaired software when it starts up.
  3. Start a new task and ask the Agent for the web request again. Tasks that were already open keep the Gateway's old list of features; a new task sees the repaired one.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows Connected and a web request in a new task returns a result instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway; the details name the missing software. Don't re-enter the website's password or key and don't delete the Gateway's pairing; neither fixes missing software.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's HTTP readiness check hit ModuleNotFoundError while importing a mandatory HTTP module (jsonschema, requests, urllib3 or a gateway_core HTTP module), so the Gateway installation is incomplete.

What this means

  • Readiness caught ModuleNotFoundError while importing mandatory native HTTP modules; only recognized dependency names are exposed publicly. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Readiness caught ModuleNotFoundError while importing mandatory native HTTP modules; only recognized dependency names are exposed publicly.

How to diagnose it

  • Check supported installer/dependency diagnostics on the selected Gateway; a missing nested module may not have a public name.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, rerun the supported installer as the account the Gateway runs under: ./install.sh (Server plus local Gateway), ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh (Linux), ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh (macOS) or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 (Windows). Require its dependency audit to pass, restart the Gateway after active jobs are settled, refresh Gateway metadata and start a new task.
  • Reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata.
  • From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Require the installer dependency audit and local functional checks to pass, then verify the selected Gateway advertises the required capability. Start a new task after refreshing metadata; existing tasks retain their captured capability snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • Required imports and native HTTP readiness pass after repair on that host.

What not to do

  • Do not enter target API credentials to repair a missing Gateway dependency.
  • Do not restart a Gateway with unsettled mutations without first reconciling its active work.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
